title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Cinsault
objectives: Know how long to keep it

steps.title: Light food
steps.body: Cinsault's light body and soft tannin suit Mediterranean food: grilled fish, salads, charcuterie, roast chicken, mezze and tapas. Rosé suits seafood, salads and summer lunches. Its fruitiness handles mild spice, like Moroccan tagines or Lebanese dishes.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve red Cinsault slightly cool, 13 to 15 degrees, and rosé at 8 to 10. Most is best young, within two to three years. Old-vine wines and blends like Château Musar can age much longer.

steps.prompt: What temperature suits a red Cinsault?
steps.explanation: Slightly cool brings out its fruit and freshness.

steps.body: Château Musar, from Lebanon, blends Cinsault with Cabernet Sauvignon and Carignan, and can age for decades. It's a rare chance to taste old Cinsault.

steps.prompt: Most Cinsault is made for long ageing.
steps.explanation: Not true. Most is best young, though some blends and old-vine wines age.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cinsault suits Mediterranean food, mezze and grilled fish
Serve red slightly cool and rosé chilled
